name: fs-operation-scope-enforced
body: Law (prose; assessed by review): a filesystem operation (`apg_rm` / `apg_mv` / `apg_cp`) may touch ONLY a path the acting agent's EFFECTIVE `edit`-action rules permit — the source path, and for mv/cp the destination path as well. The TOOL enforces this by asserting the `edit` action with the resolved target path as the resource through opencode 2.x's permission surface — the mechanism `requirements.constraint.agent-fs-per-path-permission` states — so opencode's ordered `edit` matching (the lower-priority configuration, the global rules, and the agent's own entries, LAST matching entry winning) decides the path; the tool lets a denial or a rejection refuse the operation (fail-closed). A deny rule the `edit` action honours also refuses the fs operation, so the fs scope tracks the effective `edit` scope. The boundary is the PROJECT WORKTREE: for a code-writer, a path that resolves into the main checkout (outside every project worktree) is refused regardless of the caller-supplied directory, and `external_directory` governs a path outside the active Location and its project worktree; no operation may cross the project/worktree boundary. The capability is never granted as a blanket `"*": allow`: the grant is deny-by-default with the role's owned globs allowed under `apg/.worktrees/*/` only. The tools perform plain filesystem operations only — they are not `git rm`/`git mv` — and they never mutate graph nodes (that is `apg node rm` / `apg edge rm`).
